hook.line: Same verb, two pasts, two different stories. Rosa closed the café at six every day for forty years; last night Tomás closed it once, at ten. Spanish tells you which by the ending.
hook.es: Rosa cerraba el café a las seis. Anoche Tomás lo cerró a las diez.
hook.en: Rosa used to close the café at six. Last night Tomás closed it at ten.

rule:
Almost every verb has both pasts, and swapping one for the other changes the story.

The describing past (*-aba*, *-ía*, *era*, *iba*): it was going on, it used to happen, that's how it was. No start or finish in view.

The event past (*-é*, *-ó*, *fue*, *fui*): it happened and it's done. A dot on the timeline.

So *comía a las dos* is a habit, and *comí a las dos* is one lunch. *Llovía cuando llegué* sets a scene; *llovió toda la noche* wraps a whole night up as one finished thing.

Time words help. *Ayer*, *anoche*, *el sábado*, *de repente* point to the event past. *Siempre*, *todos los días*, *antes*, *cuando era niño* point to the describing past.

Stuck? Ask yourself: am I saying what happened, or what it was like?
smallPrint: Teachers call this the preterite versus imperfect contrast. It comes back in every review from here on.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *De niño, ___ fútbol todos los días.* (*jugué* or *jugaba*) As a boy, I played football every day.
yourTurn.answer: De niño, jugaba fútbol todos los días.
accept: De niño jugaba fútbol todos los días.
yourTurn.why: Every day as a boy is a habit, so *jugaba*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Ayer ___ fútbol con Tomás.* (*jugué* or *jugaba*) Yesterday I played football with Tomás.
yourTurn.why: One game, yesterday: the event past *jugué*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ cuando llegué.* (*Llovió* or *Llovía*) It was raining when I arrived.
yourTurn.why: The rain was already going on, so it's scene: *llovía*.

yourTurn.prompt: We used to go to the beach every year.
yourTurn.answer: Íbamos a la playa todos los años.
accept: Todos los años íbamos a la playa.
yourTurn.why: Used to, every year: the describing past *íbamos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Last night it rained a lot.
yourTurn.why: *Anoche* wraps it up as one finished night: *llovió*.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it from a habit to one time, keeping the rest: *Rosa cerraba el café a las seis.*
yourTurn.answer: Rosa cerró el café a las seis.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it from one time to a habit: *Comí a las dos.*
yourTurn.why: A habit takes the describing past: *comía*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. One visit yesterday is an event, so *fui*. *Iba* leaves the listener waiting: you were going, and then?

pitfalls.wrong: Cuando era niño, fui a la playa todos los años.
pitfalls.right: Cuando era niño, iba a la playa todos los años.
pitfalls.why: Every year as a child is a habit, so the describing past *iba*.
The rain had already started when you got there, so it's the scene: *llovía*.
